claims.claim: Faculty and students share a key complaint about discussion boards: repetitive formulaic replies.
claims.quote: Great post, <NAME>! I so agree that "<EXCERPT>".

claims.claim: Foundational issue: discussion boards sit in a discrete place in the LMS course site, separate from course content.
claims.quote: The processes of thinking, writing, and discussing occur separately from the course content.

claims.claim: Hypothesis social annotation lets students and instructors anchor questions, thoughts, resources to the text as they read.
claims.quote: anchor their questions, thoughts, and resources to the text as they read

claims.claim: Annotating while reading encourages metacognition and more authentic responses.
claims.quote: encouraging metacognition and more authentic responses

claims.claim: Students treat discussion boards as formal, distinct assignments.
claims.quote: Students often approach discussion boards as formal, distinct assignments.

claims.claim: Social annotation resembles real-time discussion, with vulnerability and thinking out loud.
Kalir: annotation is first draft thinking; people are schooled to publish only final draft.
Social annotation lets students iterate on ideas as they surface.
Annotation lets students contribute to course knowledge base by adding ideas and explanations to the text itself.
Brown and Croft: annotation lets conversation coalesce around difficult concepts; dissent has space in original context.
claims.quote: Dissenting perspectives may have a tangible space to exist in the original context

claims.claim: Annotation helps students move beyond passive reading to see themselves as scholars.
Student annotations give instructors more information for teaching decisions than responses to instructor-directed questions.
Discussion can be driven by student, instructor, or both.
Pre-class annotation shows instructors which topics or threads need attention.
Hypothesis claims replacing boards helps meet learning goals: authentic conversation, scholarly reflection, instructor visibility of understanding.
Post published 22 May 2024, 4 min read; Faculty Focus article accessed 21 May 2024.
